html:
In 1971 about ten million people fled East Pakistan into India during the Bangladesh Liberation War. It was one of the largest refugee flights of the twentieth century.

They were escaping the killings that began with Operation Searchlight in March 1971, now called the Bangladesh genocide. Hindus, whom the army targeted in particular, made up a large share. Most crossed into West Bengal, Tripura and Assam and lived in crowded camps, where cholera broke out.

India could not carry the cost for long. Indira Gandhi toured world capitals to ask for help and used the crisis as a reason to intervene, which India did in December. Abroad, the camps moved Ravi Shankar and George Harrison to hold the Concert for Bangladesh in New York in August 1971, one of the first big charity concerts. After the war most refugees went home to the new state of Bangladesh.
sum: In 1971 about ten million people fled East Pakistan into India during the Bangladesh Liberation War. It was one of the largest refugee flights of the twentieth century.
